item.title: Galaxy Evolution Can be Affected by Black Hole Jets
item.description: In recent decades, astronomers have found evidence that supermassive black holes can really mess with their galaxies' evolution. They gobble up material intended for star formation, quenching the birth of stars. Conversely, jets streaming away from those hungry monsters can also energize gas-rich regions and enhance the chances of a galaxy birthing batches of stars in those areas.

item.title: Undergraduate student may have solved puzzle regarding isolated galaxies that have stopped producing stars
item.description: An undergraduate astrophysics student at UC Berkeley has found three unusual galaxies—cataloged as Shapiro Dwarf Galaxies I, II and III. Each galaxy is far from other galaxies and has stopped making stars, a combination that is extremely rare. The discovery, published in The Astrophysical Journal, provides compelling observational evidence of a long-held astronomical theory.

item.title: Impossibly fast-moving stars are revealing the Milky Way’s mysterious heart
